events.title: Henry V Becomes King of England
events.description: Following the death of his father, Henry IV, the 26-year-old Henry V took the English throne. He soon revived England's claims in France and led the country into a new phase of the Hundred Years' War.
events.significance: His reign produced the famous victory at Agincourt in 1415. It also made him one of the best-known medieval English monarchs.

events.title: Napoleon Returns to Paris
events.description: After escaping exile on the island of Elba, Napoleon entered Paris. This began the period known as the Hundred Days, in which he ruled France again.
events.significance: His return led to the Battle of Waterloo and his final defeat and exile.

events.title: Uncle Tom's Cabin Is Published
events.description: Harriet Beecher Stowe's anti-slavery novel appeared in book form. It was a sensation and sold in huge numbers in the United States and abroad.
events.significance: The book swayed public opinion against slavery and is often cited as a factor in the tensions that led to the American Civil War.

events.title: Sarin Attack on the Tokyo Subway
events.description: Members of the Aum Shinrikyo cult released sarin nerve gas on several Tokyo subway trains during the morning rush hour. The attack killed 12 people and injured thousands.
events.significance: It was one of the deadliest acts of domestic terrorism in modern Japan. It prompted worldwide changes in how governments prepare for chemical attacks.

events.title: The Iraq War Begins
events.description: A U.S.-led coalition invaded Iraq, opening the war that toppled Saddam Hussein's government.
events.significance: The war reshaped the politics of the Middle East and remained a source of controversy for years afterward.
